races.name: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Juvenile Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Vietnorm
runners_data.note: Three-from-three in recent runs including back-to-back wins on Good, Adrian Keatley/Danny McMenamin combination in strong form (T14: 4/11), and only 20 days since last run — a lightly exposed hurdling debutant with the most compelling recent form in this field, though his natural hold-up style means he depends on a fluent jumps education.

runners_data.name: Al Za'ama
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's runner has been off 87 days and is stepping from Standard-ground handicaps where he finished 8th, 4th and 10th — the going switch to Good is fine but a fade-in-finish flag and the fact his true hold-up style has been shifted into midfield on the map both temper enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Hello Garda
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's gelding ran just five days ago — freshness is not the concern, but jumping fluency will be watched closely given the hg:p headgear marker; naturally a hold-up horse, the crowded rear group means he is unlikely to secure his ideal spot, and his Good-ground record shows zero wins from seven tries.

runners_data.name: Keep Under Wraps
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed — one run in a 17f bumper on Good (result unknown), Jack Tudor takes the ride for Greenall & Guerriero (T14: 2/8), and the U style rating reflects total uncertainty about how this horse will race over hurdles; the lightly-raced flag is the dominant caution here.

runners_data.name: Nicolai
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's runner has five consecutive finishes between 6th and 10th on Standard ground, a fade-in-finish concern, and has been off 108 days — the redistribution places him in midfield but his true hold-up style in a congested rear group makes this a very difficult pitch for him to make a winning impact.

runners_data.name: Salkadan
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton (T14: 10/35) represent a powerful team and Salkadan's one win came on Good at 12f, giving relevant going credentials; naturally a hold-up horse pressed into midfield by the field's composition, his flat form base shows he can finish — but 52 days off and the positional compromise both need monitoring.

runners_data.name: Us Officer
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's runner has been placed once from seven flat runs, was second over 17f on Good last time, and slots into the lead only because no confirmed front-runner is present — his STYLE_FIT of 0.80 reflects that he is a natural hold-up horse playing an unnatural role, and a tendency to fade if he over-exerts in front is a live risk.

runners_data.name: Zooter
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over for Jack Jones (T14: 0/17) and Zooter has a consistently honest profile — third, fourth, third, fifth, second in recent flat starts, all on or near Good/Soft ground, and genuinely suited to the 2m trip; a true hold-up type whose finishing patterns are the most reliable of the hold-up cluster, though never a winner.

runners_data.name: Adba
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's lightly-weighted runner (147lbs) has five finishes ranging from 5th to 8th with one Good-ground run, has been off 91 days, and Harry Kimber rides — the redistribution into midfield from a true hold-up style is a secondary concern; the primary issue is a consistent pattern of out-of-contention finishes with no win or place on record.

races.paceDynamic: Us Officer is the one confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the lead from a hold-up profile, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.80 will likely dictate on Good ground over 2m at Uttoxeter without any natural front-runner to pressure him — the result is a sustainable, uncontested gallop that is unlikely to be truly searching. The field behind is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types: Salkadan, Nicolai, Hello Garda, Adba and Al Za'ama are all genuine come-from-behind horses redistributed into midfield because there is simply nowhere near enough natural pace in front of them to fill the map correctly. Vietnorm (true hold-up, three recent wins) and Zooter (consistent placer, Good ground form) are the runners most naturally suited to racing off an even pace and finishing with purpose from the rear. This race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel smoothly behind the uncontested pace, jump fluently through the hurdles, and produce a sustained late run — the profile that benefits most is an athletic hold-up performer with proven Good-ground finishing ability, as the pace will be moderate enough to set up a proper staying finish rather than a race of attrition.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Us Officer sets an uncontested moderate gallop and the race develops into a stamina-test from the third-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Us Officer bowls along alone, the field settles in a compact group behind him, and the final two hurdles become the decisive phase as the strongest finishers from the mid-to-rear group sweep through. Horses with proven Good-ground finishing form and genuine hold-up profiles — rather than those redistributed out of position — profit most here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Salkadan Powers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Salkadan, despite racing out of his natural role, travels prominently enough to pinch a position and unleashes a strong run on his one win on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Dan Skelton's charge won on Good at 12f and has placed on similar ground, and Harry Skelton can coax him into a more prominent midfield berth than his redistribution suggests; a truly moderate pace would play to his stamina. If he settles mid-division rather than being buried at the back, his class in this juvenile field could tell late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Vietnorm Leads Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Vietnorm's connections elect to ride more positively than his hold-up tag implies, challenging Us Officer for the lead and converting his hat-trick of flat wins into an aggressive front-end display.
scenarios.body: Three consecutive wins including recent Good-ground victories show undeniable ability, and Danny McMenamin may opt to use that flat speed to take a prominent position on a weak pace; if Vietnorm jumps fluently this could become a two-horse battle from the front. This scenario effectively turns the race into a match between the two most forward-placed horses and leaves the hold-up cluster chasing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If Us Officer fades sharply in the final half-mile and the genuinely redistributed hold-up types — Adba, Nicolai, Al Za'ama — all arrive at once from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires that several horses racing out of role still manage to find their natural back-end position and that the pace collapses completely; given their consistent mid-to-rear finishes on the flat and lack of hurdles form, a coordinated late sweep is possible but the lowest-probability outcome. Al Za'ama's fade-in-finish warning and Nicolai's repeated poor finishes on Standard ground make this genuinely unlikely to produce a mass late challenge of quality.

watchPoints.text: Us Officer — if he jumps poorly at an early hurdle and loses his uncontested lead, the entire pace structure collapses and the race could develop into chaos, dramatically altering which finishing style benefits.

Vietnorm — watch his jumping closely on hurdles debut; three flat wins on Good give him ability credentials but a single novice error at pace could drop him out of contention irreversibly given his hold-up role.

Salkadan and Hello Garda — both natural hold-up horses likely to be jostling for the same midfield-to-rear position early; a crowded break could compromise both and any significant bumping incident should be noted for stewards.

Keep Under Wraps — complete unknown over hurdles, and Jack Tudor may need to nurse him through the early obstacles; his first-time jumping behaviour in a 9-runner field with modest pace could make him either a danger or a faller risk worth monitoring.

Zooter with Sean Bowen — the booking of a top clasp jockey for a trainer with zero wins in 17 days (T14: 0/17) suggests connections are trying to sharpen this consistent non-winner; watch whether Bowen elects to ride closer to the pace than the horse's natural profile suggests.

races.name: Roys Ices Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Miss Oreo
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up mare in poor recent form (PP last two), wearing a hood, and rated 98 — the class in the field on paper but form strings are deeply uninspiring and a stop-start hold-up style is the wrong tool for a steady-paced affair.|

runners_data.name: Miracles Do Happen
runners_data.note: Billy Aprahamian's trainer strike rate is hot at 2/3 over 14 days, and this 5-year-old won over this exact trip on Good last time — a hold-up type by style but the form suggests she has enough tactical speed to land a challenge if the pace quickens.|

runners_data.name: No Risk Today
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, returning off just 16 days for Fergal O'Brien; found a flat 2m last time and won't be pressured here — uncontested lead is a significant asset on Good ground, though she has not won yet.|

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor is a high-quality booking for Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero's filly, who has won twice over this exact trip on Good going — hold-up on the style map but recent form shows she races prominently when able; the Good ground record (2W2P from 3 starts) is the standout stat.|

runners_data.name: Culligran
runners_data.note: The only other horse with a naturally prominent style, Kielan Woods will look to slot in second and make this a true test — his best form comes over further (2m4f-2m5f) so the question is whether 2m on Good is sharp enough for him.|

runners_data.name: Curious Mrs Fox
runners_data.note: David Thompson's 5-year-old is a genuine hold-up mare whose form shows consistent mid-division placings — she's been pushed into the midfield map position because the field is rear-heavy, meaning she's unlikely to get her preferred late-run setup cleanly.|

runners_data.name: Lady Fortune
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on Good last time out for F Brennan, and again at 2m4f — a notably versatile stayer who has shown she can win with both waiting and front-running tactics; the 11-day turnaround is worth monitoring but trainer form (2/6) is solid.|

runners_data.name: Dotties Promise
runners_data.note: Susan Corbett's mare has a form string of 0606-6 and has finished sixth on her last three completed runs — a true hold-up horse forced into midfield by field composition, and without a win to her name, this looks difficult.|

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: Ran just 7 days ago for Gary Hanmer and has 15/15 runs on Good — an admirably consistent mare on the going, but a natural hold-up type placed in midfield here, and four finishes of 2nd (0 wins) in recent form suggests a horse that finds one too good.|

runners_data.name: Jukebox Annie
runners_data.note: Claire Hitch's 7-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has struggled for consistency (6P-4P5) — a natural come-from-behind type reassigned to midfield, and the pattern of pulled-up runs does not inspire confidence in a field where pace may not suit.|

runners_data.name: Myfavouritesister
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride on Patrick Neville's mare, who has run exclusively over longer trips (2m4f-3m) recently — dropping back to 2m looks a concern for a hold-up horse who needs time and distance to get competitive.|

runners_data.name: Granny B
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (hood) and returns off 11 days for M Mullineaux — form of 63-P57 is modest, and as a natural backmarker redistributed into midfield, the short turnaround combined with inconsistent form makes this a tough assignment.|

races.paceDynamic: No Risk Today is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner mares' handicap hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground at Uttoxeter — a track that tends to stretch fields out and rewards horses who travel prominently. Culligran is the only other runner with a prominent profile and will look to sit just off the pace, while Prettylady and Lady Fortune have strong form on Good ground and will be seeking a position close enough to pounce at the second-last. The redistribution note is important here: Curious Mrs Fox, Dotties Promise, Northern Rose, Jukebox Annie, Myfavouritesister and Granny B are all natural hold-up types shunted into the midfield map position — they are unlikely to get a clean run from the back of this field at a track where the pace is moderate, and their chances are structurally compromised. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers and horses who can track a lone, uncontested leader without getting boxed in — the tactical verdict is clear: proximity to the pace is the key, and hold-up horses face a significant challenge getting into winning contention off a steady tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: No Risk Leads, Nearest Wins
scenarios.trigger: If No Risk Today dictates a controlled pace and the race is decided by who tracks her most efficiently into the straight.
scenarios.body: No Risk Today sets a comfortable gallop, shielding herself from pressure throughout, and the winner emerges from the small group that tracked her — pace control means those nearest turn in full of running.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Culligran pushes up to press No Risk Today from an early stage, lifting the tempo and setting up a war of attrition.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop from the front creates a true test of stamina, and horses with genuine finishing kicks who have been held just off the pressure are rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Pace Injection Rewards Closer
scenarios.trigger: If No Risk Today's lead becomes untenable in the final half-mile and a mid-division horse gets a clear run through to challenge.
scenarios.body: A steady-then-quickening race shape occasionally allows one horse to thread through if the front group ties up — but given most closers here are redistributed hold-up types, this scenario is structurally harder to achieve.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Tail-Ender Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that the front group burns out and a genuine backmarker picks up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the lone, uncontested leader scenario and the fact that most natural hold-up horses here have been structurally displaced — requiring everything to go wrong for the front-runners.

watchPoints.text: No Risk Today (J: Jack Hogan) is the sole front-runner — if she breaks cleanly and gets an uncontested lead, all other runners will be racing to close a gap that may never appear on a Good-going Uttoxeter track that can be relentless from the front.

Prettylady and Lady Fortune are both on the upgrade with multiple wins on Good going over this trip — watch how quickly Jack Tudor and Isabelle Ryder respectively position them in the first half-mile, as track position off a moderate gallop will be decisive.

The redistribution cluster — Curious Mrs Fox, Dotties Promise, Northern Rose, Jukebox Annie, Myfavouritesister and Granny B — all want to race from further back than the field naturally allows; if they crowd each other at the rear, any one of them getting a clear run through is an unlikely but live danger if the front group weakens.

Miracles Do Happen (T14: 2/3) is the one hold-up horse whose stable is in sharp form and whose own last-run win over this exact trip on Good suggests she has enough tactical speed to overcome the style disadvantage — monitor her position in-running.

Culligran's natural prominence is notable in this field, but his best RPR runs have come over 2m4f+ — watch whether Kielan Woods uses him aggressively to press No Risk Today or settles for second, as the former creates a test that may not suit him either.

races.name: Cl Cleaning Services Ken Boulton Memorial Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type with strong recent form at this trip on Good ground (five runs at similar going, one win five places); Paddy Hanlon's 5lb claim is a real plus on 168lbs, though the tongue-tie adds a small unknown and 14 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's unexposed four-year-old carries a sparkling recent record — three wins from his last four completions, all at 20f on Good, and Harry Skelton aboard is a major tactical asset; the step back from 20f to 16f is worth noting, but he oozes class and finishing speed.

runners_data.name: Bright Legend
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter whose natural role suits the lone front-runner map position, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) signals he is somewhat racing outside his comfort zone here; 89 days off, a trainer running at only 2/7 over 14 days, and modest similar-going stats (9/15) temper enthusiasm beyond pace duties.

runners_data.name: Romany Brown
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with excellent similar-going figures (9/10, one win five places) and Ciaran Gethings in the saddle; ran just 11 days ago which could mean freshness or fatigue, and the recent F in form is a jumping flag to monitor at each hurdle.

runners_data.name: King Sacre
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse by nature, pushed into a midfield map slot because the rear is crowded — the redistribution means his best tactical position may not be available; modest recent similar-going record (3/8, no wins) and 49 days off make him a risk, though James Davies rides well here.

runners_data.name: Drombeg Lad
runners_data.note: Kielan Woods partners a horse with a consistent Good-ground profile at 16f (six from six on similar going, one win four places, all in the band); the prominent style is genuine and unaffected by redistribution, making him one of the most reliable tactical reads in the race.

runners_data.name: Emerald Time
runners_data.note: By inclination a prominent racer, but the field's volume of pace types has pushed him to a midfield map position he may struggle to hold; Tom Bellamy is a capable claimer-level jockey and the 5-year-old has a recent win at 16f on Good, but the STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful at 0.93.

runners_data.name: Diesel Line
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a solid similar-going record (11/15, two wins six places) who naturally wants to race forward, yet the crowded pace zone means he is mapped to midfield — Sean Bowen's positional nous could help him squeeze closer than the map suggests, but at OR 93 the class ceiling is real.

races.paceDynamic: Bright Legend is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead from the other seven, shapes to dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m at Uttoxeter. Romany Brown and Drombeg Lad are natural prominent types who will push forward early and likely sit just off Bright Legend's shoulder, creating a proper but not frantic tempo that keeps the race honest without turning it into a sprint. The field contains more prominent/hold-up types than the race shape can absorb naturally — Emerald Time, Diesel Line and King Sacre are all genuine front-to-midfield horses by inclination but will be shuffled wider in the pack because Bright Legend, Romany Brown and Drombeg Lad have prior claim on the front positions. With an uncontested pace-setter dictating from the front at a controlled gallop on fast ground, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp, late finishing kick — specifically those who can track the pace without burning petrol and produce a clean turn of foot in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bright Legend Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Bright Legend sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the genuine hold-up horses track within striking distance before finishing through.
scenarios.body: Bright Legend's lone front-running role on Good ground creates a predictable rhythm that leaves the closers with a clear target entering the straight; hold-up horses who have been patient and well-placed are able to finish past a tiring leader late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Force Honest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Romany Brown and Drombeg Lad refuse to sit and push Bright Legend into a faster gallop than intended, raising the tempo.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested early pace stretches the field and punishes horses who expend energy making up ground; those who travel economically in behind and stay on stoutly from the second-last benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Crawl, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Bright Legend deliberately drops the tempo to a very slow early pace, turning the race into a dash from the last couple of hurdles.
scenarios.body: A bunched field generates a chaotic, speed-dominated finish where positional horses and quick jumpers hold an edge; jockey craft and a well-timed move from the last flight become decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disruption — Falls or Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a key pace-setter or prominent horse exits through a fall or unseated rider, scrambling the anticipated race shape.
scenarios.body: The remaining field resets its order mid-race, handing an advantage to adaptable hold-up horses who can readjust without losing their rhythm; those with clean jumping records and patient jockeys find themselves best placed.

watchPoints.text: Ice Jet's jockey Harry Skelton has a strong record for the Skelton yard (10/35 over 14 days) and the horse's three recent wins at 20f on Good make him the most dangerous closer if he settles cleanly behind Bright Legend.
Romany Brown showed an 'F' (fall) in recent form — watch his jumping from the first hurdle; if he makes a serious error early, it could unsettle the prominent group and reshape the entire race.

Emerald Time and Diesel Line — both genuine prominent types redistributed to midfield — may attempt to push forward from the off regardless, risking a busier early pace than Bright Legend's handlers want; watch the first two flights for positional scrimmaging.
Bright Legend's 89-day absence and the trainer's modest 2/7 14-day record are worth monitoring in the paddock — any sign of fitness concern and the sustainable pace scenario weakens considerably.

King Sacre is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution; if he is allowed to drop away to his natural position at the rear early, he becomes a live each-way threat if the pace quickens late — watch where James Davies positions him leaving the start.

races.name: Sheila And Wayne Golden Wedding Anniversary Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sure Touch
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's 10-year-old has Good-ground course form and wants a prominent role; with a 39-day freshener and Tom Hutsby (10) claiming, his 8 runs on similar going show a record of 3W4P, giving him tactical flexibility to track Sony Bill without getting embroiled in the congested second rank.

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes over on the sole confirmed front-runner who has been consistent without winning (0W3P on similar going); the 11-day turnaround is tight but Faye Bramley sends out two winners in the past fortnight, and on Good ground at Uttoxeter he gets a completely uncontested lead — his best possible scenario.

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 10-year-old arrives 14 days after a win, goes 2W3P on identical going, and the tongue-tie is retained; Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable at 163lbs, and recent form reading 1-2-4-1 makes him a natural for the prominent cluster battle, with the class to win from it.

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton's seven-year-old is the form horse in this field — four wins from five runs on Good and a 6W8P record on similar conditions — the tongue-tie and cheekpieces are familiar, and 11 days since last run is a live concern on top weight at 162lbs, but the handler's in-form yard (10/35 in 14 days) offsets that.

runners_data.name: Bagheera Ginge
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies partners a horse trained within the family yard whose hold-up style is genuine and whose 14/15 runs on similar going is the most ground-experienced profile in the field; the visor is retained, and his three Good-ground wins from the back make him the natural beneficiary if the prominent battle burns energy ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Hold Your Fort
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy rides a horse whose natural inclination is to race prominently — a 3W7P record on Good ground confirms his ability — but with the race already over-subscribed at the front, he is likely to find himself in a midfield role that suits him less, tempering confidence despite solid recent form (form 1-2-3-9-5).

runners_data.name: Imperial Alex
runners_data.note: Stan Sheppard on a Tom Lacey-trained nine-year-old who goes 3W5P on Good and has won two of his last three starts at 24f; the hood is retained, and 28 days since last run is fine — he is a genuine prominent player who can legitimately claim a forward position even in a congested field.

runners_data.name: Stans The Man
runners_data.note: Ella Pickard's nine-year-old carries the blinkers and tongue-tie combination and has been running with some consistency (2W6P on similar going, 13/15), but racing only eight days after his last outing is aggressive; a natural prominent runner who will find the field too congested ahead of him, blunting the effectiveness of his preferred front-end role.

runners_data.name: The Flying Poet
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners a lightly-built seven-year-old with a striking win record on Good (2W7P from 10/11 runs on similar going, including back-to-back wins); the blinkers and tongue-tie combination is established, but 24 days since last run is straightforward — the structural issue is that his natural prominent style has no room in this field, and he will need to deliver from a position he wouldn't choose.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill is the sole confirmed front-runner and, ridden by Harry Cobden, will dictate from the front on Good ground over 3m at Uttoxeter — a trip where controlled pace-setting is a genuine asset. Behind him, Sure Touch, Grand Clermont, Sunray Shadow, and Imperial Alex all want prominent positions, creating a compressed, pressure-filled second rank that is likely to produce interference and shuffling between the 2nd and 3rd-last fences. The field carries more pace than the map can accommodate: Hold Your Fort, Stans The Man, and The Flying Poet are natural prominent racers who will be squeezed into a midfield role they did not choose, reducing their effectiveness. With Sony Bill able to set a sustainable, uncontested tempo and the prominent cluster behind him likely to race keenly and cancel each other out, this race shape strongly favours horses who can settle comfortably just off the pace or track the leader without burning energy in the prominent scrum — meaning genuine prominent types with tactical flexibility (Sunray Shadow, Grand Clermont, Imperial Alex) and any hold-up horse with the class to close (Bagheera Ginge) are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sony Bill Controls, Prompt Finishers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill dictates an honest but manageable pace and the prominent pack settles without incident.
scenarios.body: Sony Bill sets fractions that reward those tracking him efficiently, and the race develops into a staying test from 2 out where horses with strong Good-ground records at this trip come into their own; Sunray Shadow's six wins in similar conditions and Skelton horsepower make her the prime beneficiary, with Grand Clermont's two recent wins at 24f on Good also in the frame.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Boils Over Early
scenarios.trigger: If the four-runner prominent cluster races too keenly chasing Sony Bill, lifting the tempo and producing a chaotic middle section.
scenarios.body: The congested second rank burns energy fighting for position through the first circuit, and by the 3rd-last the front group is strung out; Bagheera Ginge, a genuine hold-up horse with 14 runs on similar going and three wins from the back, is the type to pick through a tired field late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill's lone lead becomes so unchallenged that he dictates a crawl and produces a powerful staying surge from the front.
scenarios.body: At 3m on Good ground with no rival willing to challenge him until too late, Harry Cobden can produce Sony Bill fresh at the last; the horse's history shows consistency rather than wins, but this uncontested scenario maximises his chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Secure Position, Shape Flips
scenarios.trigger: If Hold Your Fort or The Flying Poet successfully wrestles a prominent position and races from their natural style.
scenarios.body: This outcome is discounted because all three redistributed runners — Hold Your Fort, Stans The Man, The Flying Poet — face a structural disadvantage in a field already saturated with prominent types; should one break clear into a genuine tracking role, The Flying Poet's strong win record at 24f on Good gives him residual claims.

watchPoints.text: Sony Bill (Harry Cobden) controls this race — if he gets 400 metres of daylight and Cobden manages the fractions, every rival is racing on his terms; watch whether the prominent group makes any early attempt to close him down before the 10th fence.

Sunray Shadow and Grand Clermont are the two most likely to collide for the same rail position leaving the back straight on the second circuit — both want the prominent slot directly behind Sony Bill and a traffic incident here could end either runner's chance.

Bagheera Ginge's visor and hold-up profile mean Sam Twiston-Davies will deliberately sit last or near-last early; watch how much ground he is asked to make up from 3 out — if the pace has been genuinely slow, the closer's run may arrive too late over 3m.

Hold Your Fort and The Flying Poet, both redistributed from their natural prominent positions, are worth monitoring in the first mile for signs they are fighting for ground — if either pushes forward aggressively it will accelerate the pace materially and alter the race shape.

Imperial Alex (hood retained) is a course-and-distance-type at 24f but steps up to 3m here for the first time in recent runs — watch whether Stan Sheppard settles him conservatively early given the extra two furlongs, as any keenness on the first circuit would compromise his stamina reserves at the critical late stage.

races.name: Gary And Mavis Bird Family Raceday Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Zillow
runners_data.note: A prominent-style runner for Faye Bramley whose recent record (0F00-7) raises serious doubts about current form; Good going is not a concern but her last five runs show consistent underperformance at this level and her 28-day absence does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Shallow River
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride on this 10-year-old who won over 25f on Soft last season, but his two Good-ground prominent efforts produced only a pair of placed finishes and his last run was a modest sixth — headgear (p) suggests connections are trying to sharpen him up.

runners_data.name: Roger Pol
runners_data.note: Isabelle Ryder claims 5lb on this hold-up performer for Jamie Snowden, who has won four of his last twelve on Good ground and posted back-to-back wins at this trip — the apprentice claim and a 19-day turnaround are the only mild caveats on what looks a strong profile.

runners_data.name: Karnaval Point
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 6-year-old carries a blinder in a tongue-tie after winning two of his last three on Good ground and placed in a third; Rian Corcoran claims 5lb but this horse's jumping fluency and proven form at 2m-plus make him a natural fit for a prominent position just behind Idaho Fire.

runners_data.name: Paddy De Pole

races.paceDynamic: Idaho Fire is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious rival disputing the lead, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable but controlled gallop over this extended 2m7½f trip on Good ground. Behind him, Zillow, Shallow River, Karnaval Point, and Paddy De Pole all want prominent positions, creating genuine congestion in the chasing pack that could produce crowding and interference between the third-last and second-last hurdles. Roger Pol and Tyson sit naturally further back and are the purest hold-up threats, likely to have clear daylight once the prominent scrummage sorts itself out in the home straight. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — Karnaval Point and Paddy De Pole, with the stronger recent form and better going records, are most likely to actually land the prominent slots behind Idaho Fire, while Pike Road and Divilabother are genuine prominent horses who will almost certainly be shuffled back against their will. This race shape — an uncontested lead, a sustainable gallop on Good ground over a staying trip, and a bunched prominent pack — strongly favours horses who can stalk just off the pace in a clear position or produce a well-timed late run from midfield, making Paddy De Pole, Karnaval Point, and Roger Pol the most tactically advantaged profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Idaho Fire dictates an even gallop and the prominent pack fails to close him down before the last, setting up a true staying test.
scenarios.body: Idaho Fire controls tempo throughout, and the prominent horses who track him most cleanly — Karnaval Point and Paddy De Pole — are best placed to pounce over the final two flights on a track that rewards jumping fluency. Horses with strong Good-ground form and proven stamina at this trip dominate, while those shuffled back against their will lack the momentum to bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes traffic problems mid-race and the pace falters in the back straight, allowing hold-up horses to produce strong finishes.
scenarios.body: Roger Pol, fresh off two consecutive wins and with a dominant Good-ground record (12/15), has the class and tactical profile to pick off tiring rivals when the prominent pack burns each other out. Tyson, whose last three runs all produced top-two finishes, carries the form and a quality booking in Harry Skelton to deliver a late challenge if given a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Idaho Fire finds an unusually uncontested lead and the prominent pack is so disrupted by congestion that no horse organises a coherent challenge before the last.
scenarios.body: Idaho Fire is a lightly-weighted, in-form 5-year-old who won last time out and whose trainer James Owen has been in strong form (13/38 over 14 days); if he is simply never seriously threatened, a wire-to-wire performance at this stiff track is not impossible. The chase pack's infighting gives him the margin he needs, and none of the hold-up horses arrive with enough pace reserves to close on Good ground over this distance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Fluent Jumper Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage causes fallers or late mistakes and a horse that jumps cleanly throughout steals the scenario.
scenarios.body: Zillow has claims only if chaos reduces the field and her prominent style lands her in the right place at the right moment, but her recent form (0F00-7) makes her a rank outsider for this scenario. Divilabother — a natural front-runner squeezed into midfield against type — could benefit from a chaotic race that resets positions, though racing out of role materially reduces the likelihood this shape delivers for her.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Zillow, Shallow River, Karnaval Point, and Paddy De Pole are all chasing the same two spots behind Idaho Fire; expect significant jostling between the second and third-last hurdles that could compromise multiple runners' chances.

Divilabother ran just two days ago and, as a natural front-runner squeezed into midfield, is at double risk — watch for laboured jumping or slow responses in the back straight that could make her a risk to those around her.

Pike Road in the visor is another genuine prominent horse likely to be shuffled back; a frustrated early effort to hold position could produce erratic jumping that unsettles the compact mid-race group.

Idaho Fire sets the pace alone — if he is allowed to coast through the early stages unchallenged on Good ground, the race could be over as a contest before the home turn, with the time splits worth watching to assess whether any hold-up horse has the residual pace to close.

Roger Pol's last five runs are all on Good ground with a 4W7P record — note how cleanly Isabelle Ryder (5lb claim) settles him early; if he is held up too far back in a compact field, traffic through the final turn could be a decisive factor against him.

races.paceDynamic: Belle Le Grand is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap chase over 2m4f at Uttoxeter on Good ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead she should dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo that suits a prominent, jumping-lead style. Ras Kassar and At The Oche are likely to track her through the early stages, creating a small lead group, while the bulk of the field — Palamon, Country Park, Gateau De Miel — will be forced to cover ground from deeper. This field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can place at the rear: Lakefield Flyer, Hudson, and A Dublin Job are all natural closers redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply not enough congestion near the pace to force them forward, and they are unlikely to secure their optimal position anyway. The sustainable, uncontested gallop Belle Le Grand will set on Good ground overwhelmingly favours the prominent-to-lead profile, and horses who can travel close to the pace without expending excess energy stand to be best served by this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belle Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Le Grand leads from flag to finish at a controlled clip and no rival applies meaningful pressure through the back straight.
scenarios.body: Belle Le Grand stamps her authority jumping cleanly, the modest pace suits horses who can travel close to her, and Ras Kassar or At The Oche — both prominent types tracking the leader — hit the line strongly with a rhythm established throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind Clear
scenarios.trigger: If At The Oche or Ras Kassar move up to challenge Belle Le Grand from the fourth-last, turning it into a jumping duel that grinds out the weakest.
scenarios.body: A sustained mid-race move by the tracking prominent types drains the leader and sets up a finish between horses who pinged their fences and conserved energy through a steady first circuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Nicks It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough early to cut Belle Le Grand's throat, leaving the closers with ground to make up but a floundering field ahead of them.
scenarios.body: Country Park or Gateau De Miel, both proven on Good ground and carrying course form, pick off the toiling front two in the run-in, though this scenario requires more pace than this field realistically generates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race somehow develops a strong enough gallop to bring the redistributed rear-group types into play in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Lakefield Flyer or Hudson would need to find themselves much closer than their natural style typically places them, and with a STYLE_FIT discount applied to both, this scenario depends on an atypical race shape that the single front-runner setup makes unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Belle Le Grand is the pivot of the entire race shape — if she jumps untidily at any of the early fences or gets pushed into a faster-than-comfortable pace, the dominant Scenario A collapses and the race opens up dramatically.|

Buddah Castle's back-to-back unfinished runs (UU) make Brian Hughes's early jumping critical to watch — a third refusal or fall could cause interference for horses immediately behind him in a 10-runner field.|

At The Oche has been placed in five of six recent starts without winning — if he travels smoothly into contention again, the key tactical question is whether Harry Skelton can produce a different finish that converts position into victory.|

The three redistributed hold-up runners (Lakefield Flyer, Hudson, A Dublin Job) are worth monitoring for traffic issues in the back straight — if they are caught wide or stuck in tight, their chances are further compromised beyond the pace-shape discount already applied.|

Country Park and Gateau De Miel are both proven on Good turf but both need pace; if Belle Le Grand crawls the first mile, watch for either Jonjo O'Neill Jr. or Tom Broughton making an uncharacteristically early move to manufacture the run they need.|

races.paceDynamic: Iamyouare is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m4f at Uttoxeter. Pure Logic and Luminaries will push to be prominent behind, giving the pace-setter a clear lead without being seriously pressured early. This controlled, single-pace scenario strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile that can control the tempo, jump well throughout, and grind out the finish before hold-up horses can close — making front-to-prominent runners the primary beneficiaries. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can honestly accommodate: Beny Nahar Road, Crafty Gael, Warner's Cross, and Illico De Montave are genuine hold-up horses displaced to midfield on the map, and of those Jafimgoso and Royal Rocket are best placed to secure a realistic forward position compared to the others.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iamyouare Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Iamyouare leads from the front and sets a measured, uncontested gallop that saps the finishing kick of hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Iamyouare dictates the fractions without pressure, jumping fluently and stretching the field on the final circuit before the hold-up pack can mount a meaningful challenge from deep; the prominent horses who track closely are best positioned to exploit any late fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces

scenarios.body: Pure Logic or Luminaries track Iamyouare at close quarters, use a sound jumping platform to travel well throughout, and pick up decisively when the leader's stride shortens; the moderate weight carried by Luminaries and Pure Logic suits if the pace has genuinely taken a toll on Iamyouare.

scenarios.body: A messy, competitive gallop causes Iamyouare to capitulate before the home turn and compresses the field, allowing a midfield horse to benefit from the resulting blanket finish; this is unlikely given only one genuine front-runner and the modest ratings of those who might press.

watchPoints.text: Iamyouare's jumping is critical — a single error at a hurdle early on could cost the lead and fundamentally alter the race shape that this entire analysis depends upon; watch it closely from the flag.

Pure Logic and Luminaries both have prominent tendencies and could pressure Iamyouare harder than expected in the first mile, inadvertently creating the stronger pace that benefits hold-up horses like Jafimgoso.
Jafimgoso's last run produced a 4th on Good over 26f — if Harry Skelton elects to ride more positively than usual given the expected slow pace, it could be a live danger rather than a late closer.
Illico De Montave's 329-day absence makes it an unknown quantity at this trip and going — any signs of freshness or erratic jumping could disrupt the midfield runners around it in the early stages.

Beny Nahar Road is tagged with tongue-strap headgear and has a sharply declining form profile (0 twice recently) despite good earlier form — Hamilton may attempt to place it more aggressively than its true style warrants, adding minor pace pressure.

races.paceDynamic: Fiskardo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no credible rival to push him from the front, he is likely to control proceedings at a sustainable gallop over the 2m4f trip on Good ground at Uttoxeter. October Hill and Tommy Cullen are the nearest prominent types, but neither shapes as a natural pace-presser, so Fiskardo should dictate comfortably without being harassed through the early and middle stages. The pack behind him is dominated by hold-up horses — Uhtred Ragnarson, Sonyourastar, The Secret Pearl, Ashdown Forest, Papillondelumiere and Mc'flo all prefer to come from off the pace — meaning the race will likely string out steadily before a single late surge from the chasing group. This shape — a lone, uncontested front-runner setting a measured tempo — strongly favours prominent-to-mid-division horses with a strong staying finish, particularly those who can travel in the slipstream and attack from second or third, rather than deep closers who need a truly searching gallop to get competitive. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; The Secret Pearl, Ashdown Forest, Papillondelumiere and Mc'flo are the runners most likely to find themselves racing out of their natural position, with Uhtred Ragnarson and Sonyourastar best placed to secure the genuine back-end berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fiskardo Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Fiskardo is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a fair but not punishing gallop, conserving enough for a strong finish.
scenarios.body: Fiskardo dictates the fractions entirely on his own terms, turning for home in a prime position with a lead he can defend; his Good-ground form record (three placed efforts at this track) backs the stamina angle over 2m4f. Prominent racers who can latch on early — October Hill in particular — are best positioned to mount a challenge, but face the task of closing a gap they never fully opened.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late

scenarios.body: Uhtred Ragnarson or Tommy Cullen, tracking within striking range throughout, sees a split in the closing stages and powers past a tiring Fiskardo on the run-in; Good ground suits both and neither has been asked for an early effort. This scenario rewards horses with strong finishing form at this trip rather than deep closers needing a true test.

scenarios.label: C

scenarios.body: Sonyourastar, under Sean Bowen, or Ashdown Forest under Harry Skelton, benefits from a wall of beaten horses presenting a clear late run; both have shown ability in Good conditions and carry yard confidence. However, both The Secret Pearl and Ashdown Forest are racing out of their natural hold-up roles by map placement, reducing the probability this scenario delivers cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Finish, Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down tactically — Fiskardo overpaces himself or falls, causing positional chaos — opening the race up to a low-rated runner.
scenarios.body: Papillondelumiere or Mc'flo, largely unexposed at this trip and without the weight burden of rivals, could steal into contention if the field is caught flat-footed; Mc'flo has a complete absence of Good-ground wins but benefits from carrying minimum weight. This remains a low-probability outcome heavily dependent on race incidents rather than pure ability.

watchPoints.text: Fiskardo sets the entire race tempo alone — if he is allowed to bowl along without being challenged, his lead could prove insurmountable; watch for any horse attempting to close the gap going to the third-last hurdle, as this is the critical moment where the race will be decided.

Ashdown Forest returns just two days after her last run and steps up significantly in trip to 2m4f — the quick turnaround for Dan Skelton's four-year-old is a significant physiological flag, and if she is not finishing strongly in the home straight her run should be treated with caution for future reference.

The Secret Pearl, Ashdown Forest, Papillondelumiere and Mc'flo are all natural hold-up horses likely to find themselves racing out of position in a compressed midfield — watch for traffic problems or interference approaching the home turn as this cluster of similar-styled runners attempts to find racing room simultaneously.

October Hill's tongue-tie and cheekpieces combination has been running throughout his recent form — if David Pipe has freshened him after 45 days and he travels prominently early, his Uttoxeter course form over a longer trip is a positive benchmark worth tracking from the front of the chasing pack.|
